title: Choose the visual world for Agent Kanban
question: One direction is fully worked out below. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll for a fresh hand.

options.label: Transit Map
options.lineage: Vignelli's 1972 subway diagram, Unimark signage, Beck's Underground map
options.thesis: Every task rides a line: the eight columns are stations, and each agent runs its own lettered, colored route.
options.viewport: A black signage band on top; one thick route line strings the eight stations with live counts; cards hang below as service tiles with agent route bullets, next stops and departure countdowns.
options.risk: Turns into a transit costume if the line stops carrying real state; the light ground also needs its night-service twin for late hours.

raised.raise: Blocked and unavailable things wear a diagonal hatch, so state never rides on color alone.
Priority reads as a fixed size ramp on the route bullet, urgent largest, not only as a color.
Every automatic move is shown before it happens: each card names its next stop and when it leaves.
Browse and edit are one object: title, assignee and priority edit in place on the board.
On a small screen one field stays dominant: the live stations take the view and the rest fold to markers.
The frame is the grid: the route line that links the stations also aligns the whole board.

options.label: Flight Strip Bay
options.lineage: air traffic control flight progress strips and radar scopes
options.thesis: Every run is a printed flight strip slid from bay to bay, so a whole sky of agents reads in one sweep.
options.viewport: A dark scope room: eight strip bays side by side, each run a strip with callsign, route and times, and a slim radar ring marking every running agent.
options.risk: Familiar: it sits close to the dark control-room look most agent dashboards already ship.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.lineage: industrial streetwear: quoted caps, zip-tie tags, hazard stripes
options.thesis: Every zone named literally in quotes, the active thing tagged in safety orange.
options.viewport: Stenciled crate-label cards in quoted caps, BLOCKED under a hazard stripe, the running card tagged orange.
options.case: Fuses cleanly (hazard = blocked, tag = active) but the audience is not streetwear, and quoted condensed caps tire the eye over a long day.
options.risk: Shouts at a surface that is open all day.
options.kept: State encoded in pattern: blocked and unavailable things wear a diagonal hatch.

options.label: Star Atlas Chart
options.lineage: celestial star atlases and night-vision field charts
options.thesis: Tasks plotted as stars by importance, parent chains drawn as constellations.
options.viewport: A navy chart where each task is a star sized by priority and linked tasks form constellations.
options.case: Fits the late-night sessions, but a star field does not show how work flows from idea to done.
options.risk: Beautiful at a glance, slow to act on.
options.kept: Importance as a fixed magnitude ramp: priority reads as bullet size.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Work moves through fixed stations in order, each step timed and final.
options.viewport: Stations from compose to dry under amber light, each run developing into view.
options.case: Stations in order map well, but an amber monochrome drowns status colors and strains reading.
options.kept: Commit points are marked: every card shows its next stop before it moves.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Black-and-white cards that you read and edit in the same place.
options.viewport: A stack of one-bit cards linked by hand-drawn buttons.
options.case: Nostalgic for developers, but one-bit black and white cannot show status at a glance.
options.kept: Browse and edit are one object: edit cards in place on the board.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.thesis: Tasks fall like colored rain toward the agent that pulls them.
options.viewport: A dusk garden where each agent is a cloud and tasks rain toward it.
options.case: Memorable, but neither the owner's world nor a clear way to operate a queue.
options.kept: One field stays dominant on small screens.

options.label: Starship Elbow Panel
options.thesis: The whole app framed by sweeping pastel elbows on black glass.
options.viewport: Pastel elbows frame the board; sections are color banks; numeric codes label every button.
options.case: Fun for a sci-fi fan, but numeric-code labels fail the any-skill-level test.
options.kept: The frame is the grid: one structural line aligns everything.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark, fast developer board in the Linear and Raycast mold, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A dark sidebar, eight compact columns of rounded cards, and a command palette.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the tools it sits beside, by design.

seed.outcome: Transit Map (candidate 5 of 7) assigned; the owner then pinned their crest world, which carries the Transit Map topology.
